title: The Novel: Plot, Character and Narration
summary: Elements of the novel: plot structure, conflict, characterisation, setting, narrative point of view, theme and symbol, with an original extract for practice.

items: **Climax**: the turning point of greatest tension.
**Falling action**: the consequences of the climax.
**Resolution (denouement)**: the conflict is resolved or the story closes.

rows: A boy struggles with guilt over a lie
Two rivals compete for the captaincy
A girl defies her community's expectations

notes.text: Writers reveal character **directly** (the narrator tells us: 'She was generous') and **indirectly** through speech, actions, thoughts, appearance and how others react. A **protagonist** is the main character; the **antagonist** opposes them. **Round** characters are complex and change (**dynamic**); **flat** characters are simple and stay the same (**static**).

items: **First person** ('I'): we see only what the narrator knows; may be **unreliable**.
**Third person limited**: follows one character's thoughts.
**Third person omniscient**: an all-knowing narrator who can enter any character's mind.

notes.title: Practice extract (written for FreeSheet)
notes.text:
Ayanda had promised herself she would not cry at the station. She kept the promise until the train began to move and she saw her grandmother on the platform, small in her blue coat, waving a handkerchief as though she were directing traffic. Then the tears came, hot and embarrassing, and the man opposite pretended to read his newspaper.

She had never been further than Mthatha. Now she was going to Johannesburg, to a school with a library bigger than her whole village, and she did not know a single person there. She touched the envelope in her pocket: her grandmother's letter, which she had been told not to open until she arrived.

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: In contextual questions, refer to the extract AND to the rest of the novel. When asked about character, give the trait (an adjective) and then the evidence.

questions.prompt: What is the turning point of greatest tension in a plot called?
From which point of view is the practice extract told?
Ayanda's struggle not to cry is an example of…
A dynamic character changes during the story.
An omniscient narrator can only report one character's thoughts.
Match each plot stage to its description.
What does the simile 'as though she were directing traffic' suggest about the grandmother?
questions.memo:
✓ She waves energetically/vigorously (1)
✓ suggesting her strong love and determination, even humour in a sad moment (1)

questions.prompt: Why does the man opposite 'pretend to read his newspaper'?
questions.memo:
✓ He notices Ayanda crying (1)
✓ and pretends not to, to spare her embarrassment (1)

questions.prompt: What does 'a library bigger than her whole village' show about Ayanda's new life?
questions.memo:
✓ Hyperbole/contrast (1)
✓ showing how different and overwhelming the city school will be compared with home (1)

questions.prompt: How does the writer create suspense at the end of the extract?
questions.memo:
✓ The unopened letter (1)
✓ makes the reader wonder what the grandmother has written (1)
